title.zh: 卷361 列傳一百四十八 刘清 傅鼐 严如熤子：正基
title.en: Volume 361 Biographies 148: Liu Qing, Fu Nai, Yan Ruyi son: Zheng Ji
title.raw: 卷361 列傳一百四十八 刘清 傅鼐 严如熤子：正基

sentences.zh: 列傳一百四十八

translations.literal: Biographies 148
translations.idiomatic: Biography 148

sentences.zh: 劉清傅鼐嚴如熤子正基

translations.literal: Liu Qing, Fu Nai, Yan Ruyi's son Zheng Ji
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qing, Fu Nai, and Yan Ruyi's son Zheng Ji

sentences.zh: 劉清，字天一，貴州廣順人。

translations.literal: Liu Qing, courtesy name Tianyi, was a native of Guangshun in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qing, style name Tianyi, came from Guangshun in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 由拔貢議敘，授四川冕寧縣丞，擢南充知縣，政聲為一省之冠。

translations.literal: Through the juren selection process for official rank, he was appointed assistant magistrate of Minning in Sichuan, then promoted to magistrate of Nanchong; his reputation for governance ranked first in the province.
translations.idiomatic: Selected through the juren quota for appointment, he was made assistant magistrate of Minning in Sichuan and then promoted to magistrate of Nanchong, where his administrative reputation stood at the top of the province.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，教匪起，清得民心，募鄉勇五百人擊賊，人樂為用。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing, when the sect rebels rose, Qing won the people's hearts, recruited five hundred militia to attack the bandits, and men were glad to serve under him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Jiaqing reign, when sectarian rebels broke out, Qing won popular trust, raised five hundred local militia to strike the rebels, and men were eager to follow him.

sentences.zh: 賊自為民時知其名，遇輒避之。

translations.literal: The bandits had known his name since they were commoners, and whenever they met him they would avoid him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had known his name even when they were ordinary people, and they would turn aside whenever they encountered him.

sentences.zh: 繼從總督英善剿達州匪徐天德，數捷，率鄉勇羅思舉赴賊營諭降羅其清，未得要領；

translations.literal: He then followed Governor-General Yingshan in suppressing Xu Tiande, the rebel of Dazhou, winning several victories; he led the militiaman Luo Siju to the rebel camp to persuade Luo Qiqing to surrender, but did not obtain a clear agreement;
translations.idiomatic: He next served under Governor-General Yingshan against Xu Tiande, the Dazhou rebel, and won repeated victories. He sent the militia leader Luo Siju to the rebel camp to negotiate the surrender of Luo Qiqing, but no definite terms were reached;

sentences.zh: 而徐天德與王三槐、冷天祿合陷東鄉，二年春，始復之，遂署東鄉。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Xu Tiande, together with Wang Sanhuai and Leng Tianlu, jointly seized Dongxiang; in the spring of the second year it was recovered, and Qing was appointed to administer Dongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Xu Tiande joined Wang Sanhuai and Leng Tianlu in capturing Dongxiang. In the spring of the second year Qing helped recover it and was put in charge of the district.

sentences.zh: 進克清谿場，擒賊黨王學禮，天德之舅也，言天德與王三槐皆有歸順意。

translations.literal: Advancing, he captured Qingxi Field, seized the rebel partisan Wang Xueli—Xu Tiande's maternal uncle—who said that both Xu Tiande and Wang Sanhuai wished to submit.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced and took Qingxi Field, capturing the rebel Wang Xueli, Xu Tiande's uncle, who reported that both Xu Tiande and Wang Sanhuai were willing to surrender.

sentences.zh: 總督宜綿令清往招三槐，遍歷諸賊壘，迎送奉酒食甚謹，宣示招撫，皆聽命，夜宿其帳中。

translations.literal: Governor-General Yimian ordered Qing to go and win over Wang Sanhuai; he visited every rebel stronghold, was received and sent off with great care and offerings of food and drink, proclaimed the policy of pacification, and all obeyed; he even spent nights in their tents.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Yimian sent Qing to negotiate with Wang Sanhuai. He toured every rebel camp, was escorted in and out with scrupulous hospitality, announced the government's offer of amnesty, and found them all compliant—even sleeping in their tents at night.

sentences.zh: 三槐隨至大營，約期率所部出降，然實藉覘虛實，非真意。

translations.literal: Sanhuai accompanied him to the main camp and agreed on a date to lead his followers out in surrender, but in fact he was using the opportunity to spy on the army's strength and had no sincere intent.
translations.idiomatic: Sanhuai came with him to headquarters and set a date to bring his men out in surrender, but he was really reconnoitering the army's strength and had no genuine intention of yielding.

sentences.zh: 屆期，三槐詭稱於雙廟投降，伏匪為掩襲計，官軍預設備，擊敗之。

translations.literal: When the day came, Sanhuai falsely claimed he would surrender at Shuangmiao and hid rebels for an ambush; the government troops had made preparations in advance and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When the appointed day arrived, Sanhuai pretended he would surrender at Shuangmiao while hiding rebels for a surprise attack. The government forces were ready and routed them.

sentences.zh: 時羅其清、冉文儔並聚方山坪，清偕總兵百祥奪多福山賊壘，會諸路兵攻方山坪，克之。

translations.literal: At that time Luo Qiqing and Ran Wenchou were both gathered at Fangshanping; Qing, together with the regional commander Baixiang, seized the rebel stockade on Duofu Mountain, joined forces from all routes in attacking Fangshanping, and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Qiqing and Ran Wenchou were then encamped together at Fangshanping. Qing joined Regional Commander Baixiang in storming the rebel stronghold on Duofu Mountain, then combined with troops from every direction to attack Fangshanping and capture it.

sentences.zh: 賊竄通江、巴州，與徐天德、王三槐合，清所部鄉勇增至千餘人，桂涵、李子青等皆驍勇善戰，偕諸軍擊賊，疊有殲獲，羅、冉二匪漸蹙。

translations.literal: The rebels fled to Tongjiang and Bazhou and joined Xu Tiande and Wang Sanhuai; Qing's militia grew to more than a thousand, and Gui Han, Li Ziqing, and others were all fierce and skilled in battle; fighting with the regular armies, they repeatedly destroyed and captured the enemy, and the two rebel bands of Luo and Ran were gradually cornered.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled into Tongjiang and Bazhou and linked up with Xu Tiande and Wang Sanhuai. Qing's militia swelled to more than a thousand men, including the formidable fighters Gui Han and Li Ziqing. Fighting alongside the regular forces, they won victory after victory, and the Luo and Ran factions were gradually driven into a corner.

sentences.zh: 三年，署廣元縣事。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed to administer Guangyuan County.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was put in charge of Guangyuan County.

sentences.zh: 總督勒保攻王三槐於安樂坪，未下，復令清往招撫。

translations.literal: Governor-General Lebao attacked Wang Sanhuai at Anleping without success and again ordered Qing to go and win him over.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Lebao besieged Wang Sanhuai at Anleping without success and again sent Qing to negotiate his surrender.

sentences.zh: 三槐恃前此出入大營無忌，留隨人劉星渠等為質，三槐遂詣軍門，勒保奏報大捷，俘三槐至京。

translations.literal: Sanhuai, relying on his earlier freedom to enter and leave the main camp without restraint, left his followers Liu Xingqu and others as hostages; Sanhuai then came to the army gate, Lebao reported a great victory, and Sanhuai was captured and sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Confident from his earlier unhindered visits to headquarters, Sanhuai left Liu Xingqu and others behind as hostages and then presented himself at the army gate. Lebao reported a great victory, and Sanhuai was taken captive to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 廷訊時，言：「官逼民反。

translations.literal: At his court interrogation he said: "Officials drove the people to rebel."
translations.idiomatic: At his interrogation before the throne he said, "The officials drove the people to rebel."

sentences.zh: 」仁宗詰之曰：「四川一省官皆不善耶？

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong questioned him: "Are all the officials in Sichuan province bad?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong pressed him: "Were every official in Sichuan corrupt?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「惟有劉青天一人。

translations.literal: He answered: "There is only one man, Liu Qingtian."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "There was only one—Liu Qingtian."

sentences.zh: 」劉青天者，川民以呼清也。

translations.literal: "Liu Qingtian" was what the people of Sichuan called Qing.
translations.idiomatic: "Liu Qingtian"—"Blue-Sky Liu"—was the name the people of Sichuan gave to Qing.

sentences.zh: 帝深嘉之，特諭曰：「朕聞劉清官聲甚好，每率眾禦敵，賊以其廉吏，往往退避引去。

translations.literal: The emperor was deeply pleased and issued a special edict: "We have heard that Liu Qing's official reputation is very good; whenever he leads the people against the enemy, the bandits, because he is an upright official, often withdraw and go away."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply pleased and issued a special instruction: "We have heard that Liu Qing enjoys an excellent reputation. Whenever he leads the people against the enemy, the rebels, recognizing him as an incorruptible official, often withdraw of their own accord."

sentences.zh: 如果始終奮勇，民情愛戴，著勒保據實保奏。

translations.literal: "If he continues to fight bravely and the people love and support him, Lebao is to report the facts and recommend him for promotion."
translations.idiomatic: "If he continues to fight bravely and retains the people's affection, Lebao is to recommend him on the basis of the facts."

sentences.zh: 」尋以清治績戰功奏上，晉秩同知直隸州，賜花翎。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Qing's administrative achievements and military merit were reported; he was promoted in rank to subprefect of Zhili Prefecture and granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Lebao reported Qing's civil and military achievements, and he was promoted to subprefect of Zhili Prefecture and awarded the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 於是劉青天之名聞天下。

translations.literal: Thus the name Liu Qingtian became known throughout the empire.
translations.idiomatic: From that point the name Liu Qingtian was known throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 四年，補忠州，加知府銜。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed to Zhongzhou and given the rank of prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was confirmed as magistrate of Zhongzhou and granted prefectural rank.

sentences.zh: 參贊額勒登保破冉天元、張子聰於竹峪關，令清於通江、巴州招撫餘匪。

translations.literal: He assisted Eledengbao in defeating Ran Tianyuan and Zhang Zicong at Zhuyu Pass and was ordered to pacify the remaining rebels in Tongjiang and Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served under Eledengbao when Ran Tianyuan and Zhang Zicong were defeated at Zhuyu Pass, then was assigned to win over the remaining rebels in Tongjiang and Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 自王三槐被誘，諸賊首皆疑憚不敢出；

translations.literal: After Wang Sanhuai had been lured in, all the rebel chiefs were suspicious and afraid to come out;
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Sanhuai had been tricked into surrender, every rebel leader was wary and refused to show himself;

sentences.zh: 然感清無他，不忍加害，每至賊營，必留宿盡禮，其脅從者先後投出二萬餘人，遣散歸農，以功加道銜。

translations.literal: yet feeling that Qing had no ulterior motive, they could not bear to harm him; whenever he came to a rebel camp they would lodge him with full courtesy; his coerced followers successively came out—more than twenty thousand—and were sent home to farm; for this merit he was given the rank of circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: but trusting that Qing meant them no harm, they would not hurt him and always received him with full hospitality whenever he entered their camps. More than twenty thousand coerced followers came out in succession and were sent home to farm. For this he was given circuit-intendant rank.

sentences.zh: 命隨副都御史廣興駐達州治軍餉，擢建昌道。

translations.literal: He was ordered to follow the vice censor-in-chief Guangxing, stationed at Dazhou to manage military supplies, and was promoted to Jianchang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to accompany Vice Censor-in-Chief Guangxing, who was stationed at Dazhou to manage military supplies, and was promoted to intendant of Jianchang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 五年，冉天元等合諸路賊渡嘉陵江，總督魁倫退守鹽亭鳳凰山，令清集民團守潼河，上下三百餘裡，多淺灘，盡撤防兵；

translations.literal: In the fifth year Ran Tianyuan and others combined rebels from all routes and crossed the Jialing River; Governor-General Kuilun retreated to defend Fenghuang Mountain at Yanting and ordered Qing to gather civilian militia to guard the Tong River for more than three hundred li up and down, where there were many shallows, and withdrew all defending troops;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Ran Tianyuan united rebels from every direction and crossed the Jialing. Governor-General Kuilun fell back to Fenghuang Mountain at Yanting and ordered Qing to rally local militia to hold the Tong River along some three hundred li of mostly shallow fords, while withdrawing all regular defenders;

sentences.zh: 清爭之，不可。

translations.literal: Qing argued against this but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Qing protested in vain.

sentences.zh: 賊果於太和鎮上游王家嘴偷渡，委罪於清，奪職，命以知縣用，留營效力。

translations.literal: The rebels did indeed ford secretly at Wangjiazui upstream from Taihe Town; blame was laid on Qing, his office was removed, he was ordered to serve as a magistrate, and was kept at camp to perform duties.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels duly crossed secretly at Wangjiazui above Taihe Town. Qing was blamed, stripped of rank, and ordered to serve only as a magistrate while remaining in camp on active duty.

sentences.zh: 既而德楞泰破賊，天元伏誅，諸路竄賊旁皇通、巴之間，勒保以清去歲招降成效，責籌安撫。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Delin'tai defeated the rebels, Tianyuan was executed, and fleeing rebels from all routes wandered between Tongjiang and Bazhou; Lebao, because of Qing's success in winning surrenders the previous year, charged him with planning pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Delin'tai soon broke the rebels and Tianyuan was executed. Fugitives from every route drifted between Tongjiang and Bazhou, and Lebao, recalling Qing's success the year before in winning surrenders, put him in charge of pacification.

sentences.zh: 時川匪父子兄弟一家中不盡習教為賊，而奔竄往來，過鄉里輒歸視。

translations.literal: At that time among Sichuan rebels not every father, son, and brother in a household had joined the sect to become bandits; they ran back and forth, and whenever they passed their native place they would return to look in on it.
translations.idiomatic: Not every member of a rebel household in Sichuan had taken up the sect and turned bandit; many shuttled back and forth and slipped home whenever they passed their native place.

sentences.zh: 清屯要隘，且剿且撫，遣人存問賊首家屬有歸誠之意者，潛令圖之，展轉相引，賊遂瓦解。

translations.literal: Qing garrisoned strategic passes, both fighting and pacifying; he sent men to inquire after the families of rebel chiefs who showed willingness to submit, secretly had them worked on, and through successive referrals the rebels gradually disintegrated.
translations.idiomatic: Qing held the key passes, alternating suppression with persuasion. He sent agents to visit the families of chiefs who showed signs of sincerity, worked on them in secret, and through a chain of introductions the rebel bands fell apart.

sentences.zh: 藍號鮮大川，巴州人，號為狡悍。

translations.literal: Xian Dachuan of the Blue Banner, a native of Bazhou, was known as crafty and fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Xian Dachuan of the Blue Banner, from Bazhou, had a reputation for cunning and ferocity.

sentences.zh: 其族人文炳、路保及黨楊似山，清皆厚卹其家，感恩原效死，乃使文炳勸大川降，不可，且與似山謀殺文炳。

translations.literal: His clansmen Wen Bing and Lu Bao and his partisan Yang Sishan—Qing all treated their families generously; grateful, they were willing to die for him; he had Wen Bing urge Dachuan to surrender, but this failed, and Dachuan even plotted with Sishan to kill Wen Bing.
translations.idiomatic: Qing lavished support on the families of his kinsmen Wen Bing and Lu Bao and of his follower Yang Sishan, who in gratitude offered their lives. He sent Wen Bing to persuade Dachuan to surrender, but Dachuan refused and even plotted with Sishan to kill Wen Bing.

sentences.zh: 似山乘間殺大川，與文炳、路保同降。

translations.literal: Sishan seized an opportunity to kill Dachuan and surrendered together with Wen Bing and Lu Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Sishan seized his chance, killed Dachuan, and surrendered together with Wen Bing and Lu Bao.

sentences.zh: 巴州匪遂滅。

translations.literal: The rebels of Bazhou were thus extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: The Bazhou rebels were thus wiped out.

sentences.zh: 六年，以功復原官，仍授建昌道。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, for his merit his original office was restored and he was again appointed to Jianchang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year his former rank was restored for his achievements and he was again made intendant of Jianchang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 七年春，破賊於南江五方坪，擒賊首李彬及辛文等，加按察使銜，尋授四川按察使。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year he defeated rebels at Wufangping in Nanjiang, captured the rebel chiefs Li Bin and Xin Wen and others, was given the rank of provincial surveillance commissioner, and soon afterward was appointed Sichuan surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventh year he routed rebels at Wufangping in Nanjiang and captured the chiefs Li Bin, Xin Wen, and others. He was given surveillance-commissioner rank and soon appointed provincial surveillance commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 敗藍號齊國典餘匪於兩河口，追擒其黨葛成勝。

translations.literal: He defeated the remaining rebels of the Blue Banner leader Qi Guodian at Lianghekou and pursued and captured his partisan Ge Chengsheng.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the remnant Blue Banner forces of Qi Guodian at Lianghekou and ran down his follower Ge Chengsheng.

sentences.zh: 諸匪以次平，大功告蕆，下部議敘。

translations.literal: The various rebels were pacified in turn, the great achievement was completed, and the matter was referred to the ministries for recording of merit.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining rebel bands were subdued one after another, the great campaign was declared complete, and the ministries were asked to record rewards.

sentences.zh: 清在軍七年，先後招降三萬餘人。

translations.literal: Qing had been in the army seven years and had successively won the surrender of more than thirty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Over seven years in the field Qing had won the surrender of more than thirty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 有業者歸鄉里，無業及有業原從者為鄉勇，後立戰功者​​三十餘人。

translations.literal: Those who had trades returned to their villages; those without trades and those who had trades but had originally followed him became militia, and more than thirty later won distinction in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Those with trades went home; those without, and those who had trades but had served under him, stayed on as militia, and more than thirty of them later distinguished themselves in battle.

sentences.zh: 其中苟崇勳、苟文耀、李彬、辛文、李世玉、趙文相，皆賊魁也。

translations.literal: Among them Gou Chongxun, Gou Wenyao, Li Bin, Xin Wen, Li Shiyu, and Zhao Wenxiang had all been rebel chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: Among them were Gou Chongxun, Gou Wenyao, Li Bin, Xin Wen, Li Shiyu, and Zhao Wenxiang—all former rebel chiefs.

sentences.zh: 崇勳即苟文通，已奏報殲斃而改名。

translations.literal: Chongxun was in fact Gou Wentong, who had already been reported as killed in action and had changed his name.
translations.idiomatic: Chongxun was in fact Gou Wentong, already reported dead in battle, who had taken a new name.

sentences.zh: 及軍事竣，當遣，清以諸人田廬焚盪，驟散將復為賊，臨行重犒之。

translations.literal: When the military affairs were concluded and they were to be dismissed, Qing, seeing that their fields and houses had been burned and that if they were suddenly dispersed they would become rebels again, on departing gave them generous rewards.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign ended and they were to be discharged, Qing feared that with their homes burned they would turn bandit again if dispersed abruptly, and on leaving gave them heavy rewards.

sentences.zh: 自向富室巨商貸金，人感其誠，多響應。

translations.literal: He himself borrowed money from wealthy households and great merchants; people were moved by his sincerity and many responded.
translations.idiomatic: He borrowed the money himself from wealthy families and great merchants; moved by his sincerity, many came forward.

sentences.zh: 事畢，積逋負至十萬。

translations.literal: When the affair was finished, his accumulated debts reached one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When all was done he owed a hundred thousand in accumulated debt.

sentences.zh: 八年，陝西餘匪自南山竄出棧道，清馳扼廣元，遣卒招撫被戕，詔斥輕信縱賊，以前功免罪，命理糧餉及搜捕餘匪、裁撤鄉勇。

translations.literal: In the eighth year remnant rebels from Shaanxi burst out of the plank road from the Southern Mountains; Qing hurried to hold Guangyuan and sent soldiers to win them over, but they were killed in battle; an edict rebuked him for lightly trusting and indulging bandits, but because of his former merit he was exempted from punishment and ordered to manage grain supplies, search out remaining rebels, and disband the militia.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Shaanxi remnant rebels broke out of the Southern Mountains along the plank road. Qing rushed to hold Guangyuan and sent men to negotiate their surrender, but they were killed in action. An edict rebuked him for trusting rebels too readily, yet his earlier service spared him punishment and he was ordered to manage supplies, hunt down stragglers, and disband the militia.

sentences.zh: 十年，事竣入覲，賜御製詩，有曰：「循吏清名遐邇傳，蜀民何幸見青天！

translations.literal: In the tenth year, when the affairs were concluded, he came to court for an audience and was granted an imperially composed poem, which read: "The upright official's good name spreads far and wide; how fortunate are the people of Shu to behold the blue sky!"
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, when his duties were finished, he was received in audience and given an imperial poem that read: "The upright magistrate's fame spreads far and wide—how fortunate are the people of Shu to behold the blue sky!"

sentences.zh: 誠心到處能和眾，本性從來不愛錢。

translations.literal: "Wherever his sincere heart goes he can harmonize the multitude; his nature from the first has never loved money."
translations.idiomatic: "Wherever his sincere heart goes he wins the people; by nature he has never loved money."

sentences.zh: 」時以異數榮之。

translations.literal: At the time he was honored with this extraordinary favor.
translations.idiomatic: At the time he was honored with this exceptional mark of favor.

sentences.zh: 丁繼母憂，去官，服闋，授山西按察使，遷布政使。

translations.literal: He mourned his stepmother's death, left office, and when the mourning period ended was appointed Shanxi surveillance commissioner and then promoted to provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his stepmother he left office, and when the mourning period ended was made surveillance commissioner of Shanxi and then provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 忤巡撫初彭齡，劾其袒護屬吏，降四級，以從四品京堂用。

translations.literal: He offended the governor Chu Pengling, who impeached him for shielding subordinate officials; he was demoted four ranks and appointed to a capital post of the fourth sub-rank.
translations.idiomatic: He clashed with Governor Chu Pengling, who impeached him for shielding subordinates. He was demoted four ranks and given a fourth-rank capital post.

sentences.zh: 清亦自陳不勝籓司之任，詔斥冒昧，降補刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: Qing also stated himself unfit for the duties of a provincial treasurer; an edict rebuked his presumption and he was demoted to fill the post of vice director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Qing also confessed himself unfit for provincial treasurer's duties. An edict rebuked his presumption and he was demoted to vice director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 熱河新設理刑司員，以清往，邊方草創，多持大體，斷獄平允，蒙民亦以青天呼之。

translations.literal: Rehe had newly established a judicial official for criminal cases, and Qing was sent there; the frontier was newly organized, and he mostly upheld broad principles; his judgments were fair and even the Mongols called him Qingtian.
translations.idiomatic: When Rehe created a new judicial post for criminal cases, Qing was sent there. The frontier was still being organized, and he generally ruled by broad principles. His judgments were fair, and the Mongols too called him Blue-Sky.

sentences.zh: 十七年，授山東鹽運使。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was appointed Shandong salt transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was appointed salt transport commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 十八年，河南教匪起，山東賊黨硃成良等應之，陷定陶、曹縣，巡撫同興恇懼，清自請將兵。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year sect rebels rose in Henan and Shandong bandits such as Zhu Chengliang responded; they seized Dingtao and Caoxian; the governor Tongxing was fearful, and Qing volunteered to lead troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year sectarian rebels broke out in Henan and Shandong partisans such as Zhu Chengliang joined them, capturing Dingtao and Caoxian. Governor Tongxing was alarmed, and Qing volunteered to take command.

sentences.zh: 承平久，兵習晏安，清躡草屩先之，以五百人敗賊於仿山，复定陶，又敗之於韓家廟，殪賊二千，進攻扈家集，縱火焚柵，賊突出皆死，誅賊首硃成良、王奇山，自滑縣奔至者並殲焉，兩閱月而事平。

translations.literal: After long peace the troops were accustomed to ease; Qing, wearing straw sandals, went ahead of them; with five hundred men he defeated the rebels at Fangshan, recovered Dingtao, defeated them again at Hanjiamiao, killed two thousand rebels, advanced to attack Hujiaji, set fire and burned the stockade, and when the rebels rushed out they all died; the rebel chiefs Zhu Chengliang and Wang Qishan were executed, and those who had fled from Huaxian were also destroyed; within two months the affair was settled.
translations.idiomatic: After long peace the troops had grown soft. Qing went ahead in straw sandals, led five hundred men to defeat the rebels at Fangshan, retook Dingtao, and routed them again at Hanjiamiao, killing two thousand. At Hujiaji he burned the stockade; the rebels who rushed out were all killed. Zhu Chengliang and Wang Qishan were executed, fugitives from Huaxian were wiped out, and within two months the rising was over.

sentences.zh: 賊初起時，煽惑甚眾，清先解散其脅從，成良勢孤不得逞，故得速定​​。

translations.literal: When the rebels first rose they had incited very many people; Qing first disbanded their coerced followers, Chengliang was isolated and could not act, and thus the situation was quickly settled.
translations.idiomatic: At first the rebels had drawn a huge following, but Qing first broke up their coerced supporters, leaving Chengliang isolated and unable to act, which allowed a swift settlement.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其以文職身先士卒，特詔褒獎，加布政使銜。

translations.literal: The emperor praised him for, though a civil official, taking the lead before the troops; a special edict commended him and he was given the rank of provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised a civil official who led from the front, issued a special commendation, and gave him provincial-treasurer rank.

sentences.zh: 尋授雲南布政使，仍留舊任。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Yunnan provincial treasurer while retaining his former post.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed provincial treasurer of Yunnan while remaining in his former post.

sentences.zh: 清性坦率，厭苛禮，不合於上官，又不耐簿書錢穀，遂乞病，上亦知之，改授山東登州鎮總兵，調曹州鎮。

translations.literal: Qing's nature was frank; he disliked rigid etiquette, did not get along with superiors, and could not endure paperwork and fiscal accounts, so he asked to retire on grounds of illness; the emperor also knew this and changed his appointment to regional commander of Dengzhou Garrison in Shandong, then transferred him to Caozhou Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Frank by nature, Qing disliked stiff ceremony, got on poorly with superiors, and had no patience for paperwork and accounts, so he asked to retire on grounds of illness. The emperor understood and made him regional commander of Dengzhou Garrison in Shandong, then transferred him to Caozhou Garrison.

sentences.zh: 道光二年，以老休致，命在籍食全俸。

translations.literal: In the second year of Daoguang he retired on account of age and was ordered to receive his full salary while at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Daoguang he retired on account of age and was granted his full salary at home.

sentences.zh: 八年，卒，賜祭葬，祀山東名宦，官其孫熾昌為兵部主事；

translations.literal: In the eighth year he died; funeral sacrifices were granted, he was enshrined among Shandong's famous officials, and his grandson Chichang was given the post of secretary in the Ministry of War;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he died. Imperial funeral rites were granted, he was entered in Shandong's shrine of distinguished officials, and his grandson Chichang was given a secretaryship in the Ministry of War;

sentences.zh: 瑩，舉人。

translations.literal: Ying was a provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: Ying had passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 傅鼐，字重庵，順天宛平人，原籍浙江山陰。

translations.literal: Fu Nai, courtesy name Chong'an, was a native of Wanping in Shuntian, with his original domicile in Shanyin, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Nai, style name Chong'an, came from Wanping in Shuntian; his ancestral home was Shanyin in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 由吏員入貲為府經歷，發雲南，擢寧洱知縣。

translations.literal: Through the clerical staff he purchased office as a prefectural registrar, was sent to Yunnan, and was promoted to magistrate of Ning'er.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as a clerk, he bought his way into a prefectural registrar's post, was posted to Yunnan, and was promoted to magistrate of Ning'er.

sentences.zh: 乾隆末，福康安徵苗疆，調赴湖南軍營司餉運，晉秩同知直隸州，賜花翎。

translations.literal: At the end of the Qianlong reign Fuk'anggan campaigned in the Miao frontier; Nai was transferred to the Hunan army camp to manage supply transport, was promoted in rank to subprefect of Zhili Prefecture, and was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Qianlong, when Fuk'anggan campaigned in the Miao country, Nai was transferred to the Hunan army to manage supplies, promoted to subprefect of Zhili Prefecture, and awarded the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，授鳳凰廳同知。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing he was appointed subprefect of Fenghuang Department.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiaqing he was made subprefect of Fenghuang Department.

sentences.zh: 治當苗衝，會大軍移徵湖北教匪，降苗要求苗地歸苗，當事議允之。

translations.literal: His jurisdiction lay in the Miao frontier; when the main army shifted to campaign against the Hubei sect rebels, the pacified Miao demanded that Miao lands be returned to the Miao, and the authorities agreed.
translations.idiomatic: His district lay on the Miao frontier. When the main army marched off against the Hubei sect rebels, the pacified Miao demanded their lands back, and the authorities agreed.

sentences.zh: 鼐知愈撫且愈驕，乃招流亡，團丁壯，於要害築碉堡，防苗出沒。

translations.literal: Nai knew that the more they were pacified the more arrogant the Miao became; he therefore gathered refugees, organized able-bodied men, and built blockhouses at strategic points to guard against Miao raids.
translations.idiomatic: Nai saw that indulgence only made the Miao bolder. He gathered refugees, mustered able-bodied men, and built blockhouses at key points to check Miao raids.

sentences.zh: 苗以死力來攻，且戰且修，閱三年而碉堡成。

translations.literal: The Miao attacked with all their strength; he fought while building, and after three years the blockhouses were completed.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao attacked with desperate force, but he fought on while building, and after three years the blockhouse line was complete.

sentences.zh: 有哨台以守望，砲台以御敵，邊牆相接百餘裡。

translations.literal: There were watch towers for lookout, artillery platforms to repel the enemy, and border walls connecting for more than a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Watch towers stood guard, artillery platforms faced the enemy, and border walls ran together for more than a hundred li.

sentences.zh: 每警，哨台舉銃角，婦女、牲畜立歸堡，環數十里皆戒嚴。

translations.literal: Whenever there was an alarm, the watch towers fired muskets and horns; women, livestock, and all immediately returned to the forts, and for several tens of li around everything was placed under strict guard.
translations.idiomatic: At every alarm the watch towers sounded muskets and horns; women and livestock were rushed into the forts, and strict guard was kept for miles around.

sentences.zh: 四年，擒苗酋吳陳受，加知府銜。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he captured the Miao chief Wu Chenshou and was given the rank of prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he captured the Miao chief Wu Chenshou and was given prefectural rank.

sentences.zh: 巡撫姜晟疏薦鼐能勝艱鉅，方治鎮筸一帶荒田，均給丁壯，請俟事竣送部。

translations.literal: Governor Jiang Sheng memorialized recommending that Nai could undertake difficult and heavy tasks; he was then reclaiming wasteland around Zhenqiong, distributing it equally among able-bodied men, and asked that he be sent to the ministry after the work was finished.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Jiang Sheng memorialized that Nai was equal to the hardest tasks, noting that he was reclaiming wasteland around Zhenqiong and distributing it among able-bodied men, and asked that he be forwarded to the ministry when the work was done.

sentences.zh: 時鎮筸左、右營黑苗最為邊患，五年，跴金塘苗出掠瀘溪，偕總兵富志那夜分三路搗其巢，伏兵隘路苟岩要擊，痛殲之，斃首逆吳尚保，苗始奪氣。

translations.literal: At that time the Black Miao of the left and right camps of Zhenqiong were the greatest frontier trouble; in the fifth year the Miao of Caijintang came out to plunder Luxi; together with Regional Commander Fu Zhina he divided into three routes at night to strike their nest, ambushed them at the narrow pass of Gouyan, inflicted a crushing defeat, killed the chief rebel Wu Shangbao, and the Miao first lost their spirit.
translations.idiomatic: The Black Miao of Zhenqiong's left and right camps were then the worst frontier menace. In the fifth year the Caijintang Miao raided Luxi. Nai joined Regional Commander Fu Zhina in a night attack in three columns on their stronghold, ambushed them at the Gouyan pass, crushed them, killed the rebel chief Wu Shangbao, and broke Miao morale.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉獎，命在任食知府俸。

translations.literal: An edict commended him and ordered that while in office he receive a prefect's salary.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised him and ordered that he draw a prefect's salary while remaining in post.

sentences.zh: 六年，貴州苗复亂，湖南環苗地東、南、北三面七百餘裡，其西二百餘裡接貴州，未設備。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the Miao of Guizhou rebelled again; Hunan surrounded the Miao territory on the east, south, and north for more than seven hundred li, while on the west more than two hundred li bordered Guizhou, where defenses had not been set up.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the Guizhou Miao rebelled again. Hunan's Miao frontier ran more than seven hundred li on the east, south, and north, while the western two hundred li bordering Guizhou had no defenses in place.

sentences.zh: 石峴苗煽十四寨糾湖南苗叛，鼐率鄉勇千五百馳赴銅仁。

translations.literal: The Shixian Miao incited fourteen stockades to rally Hunan Miao in rebellion; Nai led fifteen hundred militia in a rapid march to Tongren.
translations.idiomatic: The Shixian Miao stirred fourteen stockades to join Hunan Miao in revolt. Nai rushed to Tongren at the head of fifteen hundred militia.

sentences.zh: 貴州巡撫伊桑阿以招撫戡定上聞，各寨實尚沸然，槍械未繳。

translations.literal: Guizhou Governor Yisang'a reported to the throne that pacification had settled the matter, but in fact the stockades were still seething and firearms had not been surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou Governor Yisang'a reported that pacification had ended the trouble, but the stockades were still in turmoil and arms had not been turned in.

sentences.zh: 總督琅玕至，急檄鼐會剿崖屯溝，黔兵攻其前，鼐夜由山徑入，連破五巢。

translations.literal: When Governor-General Langgan arrived he urgently ordered Nai to join in suppressing Yaitungou; Guizhou troops attacked from the front while Nai entered by a mountain path at night and in succession stormed five nests.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Langgan arrived and urgently summoned Nai to join the attack on Yaitungou. Guizhou troops struck from the front while Nai entered by a mountain path at night and took five nests in succession.

sentences.zh: 上下湖山峽尤險，夜分兵圍攻，至次日克之，火其寨。

translations.literal: The gorge of Shangxiahu Mountain was especially perilous; he divided his forces at night to besiege it, took it the next day, and burned the stockade.
translations.idiomatic: The Shangxiahu Mountain gorge was especially dangerous. He split his forces for a night assault, took it the next day, and burned the stockade.

sentences.zh: 三日中盡破諸寨，殲苗二千有奇。

translations.literal: Within three days he had broken all the stockades and killed more than two thousand Miao.
translations.idiomatic: Within three days he had overrun every stockade and killed more than two thousand Miao.

sentences.zh: 仿湖南法，建碉堡守之。

translations.literal: Following the Hunan method, he built blockhouses to garrison the area.
translations.idiomatic: Following the Hunan model, he built blockhouses to hold the ground.

sentences.zh: 伊桑阿因冒功誤邊伏法，錄鼐功，加道銜，總理邊務，並命以苗疆道員用。

translations.literal: Yisang'a was executed for falsely claiming merit and harming the frontier; Nai's achievements were recorded, he was given circuit-intendant rank, placed in overall charge of frontier affairs, and ordered to serve as a Miao frontier circuit official.
translations.idiomatic: Yisang'a was executed for false claims that had harmed the frontier. Nai's achievements were recorded, he was given circuit-intendant rank and put in charge of frontier affairs, and ordered to serve as a Miao frontier official.

sentences.zh: 七年，丁父憂，詔鼐辦理邊防善後，民、苗悅服，難易生手，命留任。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he mourned his father's death; an edict ordered Nai to handle frontier defense and its aftermath; the people and Miao were pleased and submitted; the work would have been hard for a newcomer, and he was ordered to remain in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he entered mourning for his father. An edict ordered Nai to manage frontier defense and its aftermath; people and Miao alike were content under him, and because the work would have been hard for a newcomer he was ordered to stay on.

sentences.zh: 初，鼐建議遷永綏城於花園，副將營於茶洞，而貴州方藉永綏為聲援，尼其事。

translations.literal: Earlier Nai had proposed moving Yongshui city to Huayuan and stationing the vice commander's camp at Chadong, but Guizhou was relying on Yongshui as a supporting position and obstructed the plan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Nai had proposed moving Yongshui city to Huayuan and placing the vice commander's camp at Chadong, but Guizhou, which relied on Yongshui as a rear base, blocked the move.

sentences.zh: 至是詔琅玕察奏，乃赴銅仁面陳永綏孤懸苗中，形如釜底，有二難、三可慮；

translations.literal: At this point an edict ordered Langgan to investigate and report; Nai then went to Tongren and stated in person that Yongshui was isolated amid the Miao like the bottom of a cauldron, with two difficulties and three concerns;
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered Langgan to investigate and report. Nai went to Tongren and explained in person that Yongshui stood isolated among the Miao like the bottom of a cauldron, with two grave difficulties and three serious concerns;

sentences.zh: 並請移湖南守備於貴州邊境螺螄堡，以為犄角，乃決議移之。

translations.literal: he also asked to move the Hunan garrison commander to Luosi Fort on the Guizhou border as a supporting angle, and the move was then decided.
translations.idiomatic: he also asked to shift the Hunan garrison commander to Luosi Fort on the Guizhou border as a supporting flank, and the relocation was approved.

sentences.zh: 既而群苗率眾來爭，鼐率鄉勇深入，苗大集，環之數重，以奇計突圍出。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the Miao masses came in force to contest the move; Nai led militia deep into their territory; the Miao gathered in great numbers and surrounded him in several rings, but he broke out by a stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao then massed to resist. Nai led militia deep into their country, was surrounded in several rings, and broke out by a clever stratagem.

sentences.zh: 尋議勒繳槍械，苗酋石崇四等抗命，並阻丈田，十年，與其黨石貴銀糾眾數千來犯，敗之夯都河，追至孟陽岡，殲賊甚眾，生擒石崇四、石貴銀。

translations.literal: Soon afterward it was decided to compel the surrender of firearms; the Miao chiefs Shi Chongsi and others resisted orders and also obstructed land surveys; in the tenth year he and his partisan Shi Guiyin gathered several thousand men to attack; Nai defeated them at Hangdu River, pursued to Mengyanggang, destroyed many rebels, and captured Shi Chongsi and Shi Guiyin alive.
translations.idiomatic: A policy was then adopted to compel the surrender of arms. Chiefs such as Shi Chongsi resisted and blocked land surveys. In the tenth year Shi Chongsi and his follower Shi Guiyin mustered several thousand men to attack. Nai defeated them at Hangdu River, pursued to Mengyanggang, killed many, and took both chiefs alive.

sentences.zh: 是役因賊戕良苗，故得用苗兵深入，戰月餘，破寨十六，餘皆乞降，永綏苗遂平。

translations.literal: In this campaign, because the rebels had killed loyal Miao, he was able to use Miao troops to penetrate deeply; fighting for more than a month, he broke sixteen stockades and the rest all begged to surrender, and the Yongshui Miao were thus pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Because the rebels had killed loyal Miao, he was able to use Miao auxiliaries on deep raids. After more than a month of fighting he took sixteen stockades; the rest surrendered, and the Yongshui Miao were pacified.

sentences.zh: 廳屬高都、兩頭羊二寨皆震懾，無敢抗。

translations.literal: The two stockades of Gaodu and Liangtouyang under the department were all awed and dared not resist.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaodu and Liangtouyang stockades under his jurisdiction were cowed into submission and dared not resist.

sentences.zh: 事聞，予優敘，擢辰沅永靖道。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he received preferential recognition of merit and was promoted to Chenyuan Yongjing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When the report reached court he received exceptional recognition and was promoted to intendant of Chenyuan Yongjing Circuit.

sentences.zh: 鼐治苗專用雕剿法，大小百戰，所用僅鄉勇數千。

translations.literal: In governing the Miao Nai relied exclusively on the method of blockhouse suppression, fought more than a hundred battles large and small, and used only a few thousand militia.
translations.idiomatic: In pacifying the Miao Nai relied chiefly on blockhouse warfare, fought more than a hundred engagements large and small, and used only a few thousand militia.

sentences.zh: 苗人於穹山峭壁驀越如平地，無部伍行列，伏箐中從暗擊明，銃銳且長，隨山起伏，多命中。

translations.literal: The Miao crossed lofty mountains and sheer cliffs as if on level ground, without formations or ranks; they lay in ambush in the thickets and struck from darkness against light; their muskets were sharp and long-barreled, rising and falling with the terrain, and often hit their mark.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao crossed sheer cliffs and high mountains as if on flat ground, without formal ranks. They hid in the thickets and struck from cover; their long muskets, fired along the rise and fall of the hills, seldom missed.

sentences.zh: 鼐因苗地用苗技訓練士卒，囊沙輕走，習藤牌閃躍，狹路則用短兵。

translations.literal: Nai therefore trained his troops in Miao country by Miao methods: carrying sand sacks to run lightly, practicing rattan-shield dodging and leaping, and using short weapons in narrow paths.
translations.idiomatic: Nai trained his men in Miao country by Miao methods—running with sand-filled sacks for lightness, drilling in rattan-shield dodging, and using short weapons on narrow paths.

sentences.zh: 每戰後輒嚴汰，數年始得精卒千，號「飛隊」，風雨不亂行列，遺資道路無反顧，甘苦與共，是以能致死。

translations.literal: After every battle he strictly culled the ranks; only after several years did he obtain a thousand elite soldiers, called the "Flying Corps," who did not break formation in wind and rain, left supplies on the road without looking back, shared hardship and comfort alike, and therefore could fight to the death.
translations.idiomatic: After every battle he ruthlessly weeded out weak men. Only after several years did he have a thousand elite troops, the "Flying Corps," who kept formation in wind and rain, abandoned baggage on the road without a backward glance, and shared every hardship with their commander—men who would fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 先是議興屯田，上書巡撫高杞曰：「防邊之道，兵民相輔。

translations.literal: Previously, when garrison farming was under discussion, he memorialized the provincial governor Gao Qi, saying: "The way to defend the frontier is for soldiers and civilians to support each other.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when frontier garrison farming was debated, he wrote to Governor Gao Qi: "To defend the border, soldiers and civilians must work in tandem.

sentences.zh: 湖南苗疆，環以鳳凰、永綏、乾州、古丈坪、保靖五廳縣，犬牙相錯，營汛相距各數里。

translations.literal: The Miao borderlands of Hunan are encircled by the five departments and counties of Fenghuang, Yongshou, Qianzhou, Guzhangping, and Baojing, interlocking like dog's teeth, with garrison posts several li apart from one another.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan's Miao frontier is ringed by five prefectural units—Fenghuang, Yongshou, Qianzhou, Guzhangping, and Baojing—jigsawed together, with military posts standing several li apart.

sentences.zh: 元年班師後苗擾如故，鼐竭心籌之，制勝無如碉堡。

translations.literal: After the army withdrew in the first year, Miao disturbances continued as before; Nai devoted his whole mind to planning, and for overcoming the enemy nothing matched blockhouse fortresses.
translations.idiomatic: After the troops withdrew in the first year, Miao raids resumed unchanged. Nai threw himself into the problem and concluded that blockhouses were the surest way to prevail.

sentences.zh: 募丁壯數千，與苗從事。

translations.literal: He recruited several thousand strong young men to contend with the Miao.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited several thousand able-bodied men to take on the Miao.

sentences.zh: 來則痛擊，去則修邊，前戈矛，後邪許。

translations.literal: When they came, he struck hard; when they left, he repaired the border defenses—spears and halberds in front, work chants behind.
translations.idiomatic: When the Miao attacked, he met them with force; when they withdrew, he rebuilt the frontier—spears forward, work songs behind.

sentences.zh: 得險即守，寸步而前，然後苗銳挫望絕。

translations.literal: Seizing every defensible point, he held it and advanced inch by inch; only then were the Miao's fighting spirit broken and their hopes crushed.
translations.idiomatic: He seized and held every strong point, advancing inch by inch, until the Miao's fighting spirit broke and their hopes died.

sentences.zh: 湖南自乙卯二載用兵，耗帑七百餘萬。

translations.literal: Hunan had waged war for two years from the yimao year, consuming over seven million taels of treasury funds.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan had fought for two years since the yimao year, spending more than seven million taels from the treasury.

sentences.zh: 國家經費有常，頑苗叛服無定。

translations.literal: State revenue has its fixed limits, while the stubborn Miao rebel and submit without pattern.
translations.idiomatic: State finances are finite, but the stubborn Miao alternate between rebellion and submission with no predictable pattern.

sentences.zh: 募勇不得不散，則碉堡不得不虛；

translations.literal: When recruited braves must be dispersed, blockhouses cannot but lie empty;
translations.idiomatic: When hired braves must be discharged, the blockhouses must inevitably stand empty;

sentences.zh: 後患不得不慮，則自圖不得不亟。

translations.literal: When later troubles cannot but be feared, one's own planning cannot but be urgent.
translations.idiomatic: and when future trouble cannot be ignored, urgent measures become unavoidable.

sentences.zh: 通力合作，且耕且戰，所以招亡拯患也。

translations.literal: Pooling strength for joint effort, farming while fighting—that is how to win back the perished and rescue the afflicted.
translations.idiomatic: Pooling effort to farm and fight at once is how to reclaim the lost and relieve hardship.

sentences.zh: 均田屯丁，自養自衛，所以一勞永逸也。

translations.literal: Equitably dividing land for garrison colonists who feed and defend themselves—that is how to settle matters permanently with a single effort.
translations.idiomatic: Allotting land to colonists who provision and defend themselves is how to solve the problem once and for all.

sentences.zh: 相其距苗遠近、碉堡疏密，為屯田多少：鳳凰廳碉堡八百，需丁四千輪守，並留千人備戰，需田三萬餘畝；

translations.literal: Considering distance from Miao territory and the density of blockhouses, he set the extent of garrison farming: Fenghuang Department had eight hundred blockhouses, needing four thousand men in rotation for defense, with one thousand held in reserve for battle, requiring over thirty thousand mu of fields;
translations.idiomatic: He scaled garrison farms to distance from Miao settlements and blockhouse density: Fenghuang's eight hundred blockhouses needed four thousand rotating defenders, a thousand reserves, and over thirty thousand mu of farmland;

sentences.zh: 乾州廳碉堡九十餘，守丁八百，屯田三千餘畝；

translations.literal: Qianzhou Department had over ninety blockhouses, eight hundred garrison men, and over three thousand mu of garrison fields;
translations.idiomatic: Qianzhou: more than ninety blockhouses, eight hundred men, and over three thousand mu;

sentences.zh: 保靖縣碉堡四十餘，守丁三百，屯田千五百餘畝；

translations.literal: Baojing County had over forty blockhouses, three hundred garrison men, and over fifteen hundred mu of garrison fields;
translations.idiomatic: Baojing: over forty blockhouses, three hundred men, and fifteen hundred mu;

sentences.zh: 古丈坪廳苗馴，止設碉堡十餘，守丁百，屯田五百餘畝；

translations.literal: The Miao of Guzhangping Department were tractable; only a dozen-odd blockhouses were set up, one hundred garrison men, and over five hundred mu of garrison fields;
translations.idiomatic: Guzhangping, where the Miao were already tame, needed only a dozen blockhouses, a hundred men, and five hundred mu;

sentences.zh: 永綏廳新建碉堡百餘，留勇丁二千，亦屯田萬畝：而後邊無餘隙，環苗以成圈圍之勢，峻國防、省國計也。

translations.literal: Yongshou Department newly built over a hundred blockhouses, retaining two thousand braves, also with ten thousand mu of garrison fields: thus the rear border would have no gaps left, encircling the Miao in a ring to tighten national defense and economize on state expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: Yongshou added a hundred new blockhouses and two thousand braves with ten thousand mu—closing every gap behind the line, ringing the Miao, strengthening the frontier, and saving the treasury.

sentences.zh: 異族逼處，非碉堡無以固，碉堡非勇丁無以守，勇丁非屯田無以贍。

translations.literal: With alien peoples pressing close, without blockhouses there is no securing the position; without braves blockhouses cannot be held; without garrison fields braves cannot be provisioned.
translations.idiomatic: Alien peoples on the doorstep require blockhouses to hold ground, braves to man them, and garrison farms to feed them.

sentences.zh: 邊民瀕近鋒鏑，固原割世業而保身家；

translations.literal: Border people living near the clash of arms would naturally cut off hereditary estates to preserve their lives and property;
translations.idiomatic: Frontier families under the shadow of war would gladly surrender ancestral holdings to save their lives;

sentences.zh: 後路同資屏蔽，亦樂捐有餘以補不足。

translations.literal: Those in the rear who likewise benefited from this shield were also glad to contribute their surplus to make up others' shortfall.
translations.idiomatic: and inland communities that gained the same protection were willing to give from their surplus to cover the shortfall.

sentences.zh: 所募土丁，非其子弟即其親族。

translations.literal: The native levies recruited were either their own sons and younger brothers or their kin.
translations.idiomatic: The local militia he recruited were either men's own sons or their close kin.

sentences.zh: 距邊稍遠者，仍佃本戶輸租，視古來屯戍以客卒雜處，勢燕越矣。

translations.literal: Those slightly farther from the border still rented from their own households and paid rent, unlike the ancient garrison system in which guest soldiers were mixed together—the situation was as disparate as Yan and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Men posted farther back still farmed their own family land and paid rent to it—a far cry from the old frontier system of mixing unrelated garrison troops, as alien to one another as northerners and southerners.

sentences.zh: 與其一旦散數千驍健無業子弟流為盜賊，何如收駕輕就熟之用而不費大帑一錢？

translations.literal: Rather than one day dispersing several thousand fierce, able, unemployed sons and younger brothers who would drift into becoming bandits, how much better to harness their familiar skills without spending a single large-cash string from the treasury?
translations.idiomatic: Better to harness thousands of tough, jobless young men who already knew the work than to discharge them into banditry—and do it without spending a single string from the treasury.

sentences.zh: 惟執事圖之！

translations.literal: Only let Your Excellency consider it!
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Excellency to weigh this plan.

sentences.zh: 」於是收叛產分給無業窮苗佃種。

translations.literal: " Thereupon rebel property was seized and distributed for tenant farming to destitute Miao without livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial bore fruit: rebel estates were confiscated and leased to penniless Miao with no other means of support.

sentences.zh: 自擒石崇四，餘匪原返侵地，永綏得萬餘畝，乾州、鳳凰二廳次之，乃續墾沿邊隙地二萬畝，曰「官墾田」，贖苗質民田萬餘畝，曰「官贖田」。

translations.literal: After Shi Chongsi was captured, the remaining bandits voluntarily returned invaded land; Yongshou gained over ten thousand mu, Qianzhou and Fenghuang departments next in amount; then he continued reclaiming over twenty thousand mu of marginal borderland, called "officially reclaimed fields," and redeemed over ten thousand mu of Miao-pledged civilian land, called "officially redeemed fields."
translations.idiomatic: After the capture of Shi Chongsi, surrendered rebels returned seized land—Yongshou gained more than ten thousand mu, Qianzhou and Fenghuang somewhat less—and Nai opened another twenty thousand mu along the border as "official reclamation," while redeeming over ten thousand mu of civilian land held as Miao collateral as "official redemption."

sentences.zh: 以廩屯官授屯長，給老幼，籌補助，備犒賞，暨歲修城堡、神祠、學校、育嬰、養濟諸費。

translations.literal: From the granary garrison fields the garrison officer appointed garrison chiefs, provided for the old and young, arranged subsidies, prepared rewards, and covered annual repairs of forts, shrines, schools, orphanages, and poor relief.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue from granary garrison land paid garrison chiefs, supported the aged and young, funded subsidies and rewards, and covered annual upkeep of forts, shrines, schools, orphanages, and relief houses.

sentences.zh: 復以兵威勒交苗佔民田三萬五千餘畝，苗自獻田七千餘畝。

translations.literal: He further compelled by military might the surrender of over thirty-five thousand mu of Miao-occupied civilian land, and the Miao themselves presented over seven thousand mu.
translations.idiomatic: By force of arms he recovered more than thirty-five thousand mu of civilian land held by Miao; the Miao voluntarily yielded another seven thousand mu.

sentences.zh: 其經費田則佃租變價，屯丁田則附碉躬耕，訓練講武，設屯田守備掌之，轄於兵備道。

translations.literal: Revenue fields were rented out and their rent converted to cash; garrison men's fields were farmed in person beside the blockhouses, with military drill and training; a garrison-field defense commandant was appointed to oversee it, under the military defense circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Income fields were leased for cash rent; colonists farmed beside their blockhouses and drilled under a garrison-field commandant reporting to the circuit military intendant.

sentences.zh: 屯政舉，使兵農為一以相衛，民、苗為二以相安。

translations.literal: When garrison policy was fully implemented, soldiers and farmers became one body for mutual defense, while civilians and Miao remained two groups for mutual peace.
translations.idiomatic: With garrison policy in place, soldier and farmer became one for mutual defense, while Han and Miao remained distinct but at peace.

sentences.zh: 與官及兵民約曰：「毋擅入苗寨，毋稍役苗夫。

translations.literal: He made covenants with officials, soldiers, and civilians, saying: "Do not enter Miao stockades without authorization; do not lightly press Miao laborers into service.
translations.idiomatic: He bound officials, troops, and settlers: "Do not enter Miao villages without leave; do not press Miao men into corvée lightly.

sentences.zh: 」與苗約曰：「毋巫鬼椎牛群飲以糜財，毋挾槍矛尋睚眥釀釁。

translations.literal: " He made covenants with the Miao, saying: "Do not waste wealth on shamans, ox sacrifices, and communal drinking; do not carry muskets and spears to settle petty scores and brew trouble.
translations.idiomatic: " He bound the Miao: "Do not squander your substance on shamans, buffalo sacrifices, and drinking feasts; do not carry arms to settle grudges and stir up trouble.

sentences.zh: 」請乾、鳳、永、保四廳編立邊字號，廣鄉試中額一名；

translations.literal: " He requested that the four departments of Qian, Feng, Yong, and Bao establish frontier examination quotas, with one additional provincial graduate slot;
translations.idiomatic: " He petitioned for frontier examination quotas in Qianzhou, Fenghuang, Yongshou, and Baojing, each with one extra provincial degree;

sentences.zh: 苗生編立田字號，加中額一名，苗益感奮。

translations.literal: Miao students were assigned a separate "Tian" quota series with one additional graduate slot, and the Miao were all the more stirred to exert themselves.
translations.idiomatic: and a separate quota for Miao candidates, which stirred them to study all the harder.

sentences.zh: 十三年，屯務竣，入覲，詔曰：「傅鼐任苗疆十餘年，鋤莠安良，興利除弊，建碉堡千有餘所，屯田十二萬餘畝，收卹難民十餘萬戶，練兵八千人，收繳苗寨兵器四萬餘件；

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, when garrison affairs were completed, he came to court for an audience; the edict said: "Fu Nai has served in the Miao frontier for more than ten years, rooting out the wicked and securing the good, promoting benefit and removing harm, building over a thousand blockhouses, over one hundred twenty thousand mu of garrison fields, receiving and succoring over one hundred thousand refugee households, drilling eight thousand troops, and collecting over forty thousand weapons from Miao stockades;
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, with the garrison project complete, he presented himself at court. The Emperor's edict read: "Fu Nai has served on the Miao frontier for more than ten years—clearing out ruffians, protecting the peaceable, promoting what helps and abolishing what harms. He has built more than a thousand blockhouses and opened a hundred and twenty thousand mu of garrison land; succored more than a hundred thousand refugee households; trained eight thousand troops; and collected more than forty thousand weapons from Miao villages;

sentences.zh: 又多方化導，設書院六，義學百，近日苗民向學，革面革心。

translations.literal: He has also guided them by many means, establishing six academies and a hundred charity schools; recently Miao people have turned to learning, transforming face and heart.
translations.idiomatic: he has guided them by every means, founding six academies and a hundred charity schools. Lately the Miao have turned to learning and shown a change of heart.

sentences.zh: 朕久聞其任勞任怨，不顧身家。

translations.literal: We have long heard that he bears labor and blame without complaint and does not regard his own person.
translations.idiomatic: We have long heard that he bears every hardship without complaint and never spares himself.

sentences.zh: 今召見，果安詳諳練，明白誠實，洵為傑出之才，堪為岩疆保障。

translations.literal: Now summoned to audience, he is indeed composed, thoroughly practiced, clear and honest—a truly outstanding talent fit to be the bulwark of a strategic frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Now that We have met him, he proves composed, seasoned, candid, and honest—a truly outstanding man fit to guard a critical frontier.

sentences.zh: 其加按察使銜，以風有位。

translations.literal: Let him be given the rank of surveillance commissioner as encouragement to those in office.
translations.idiomatic: Grant him the rank of surveillance commissioner, as an example to officials everywhere.

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark of the edict.

sentences.zh: 十四年，擢湖南按察使。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, he was promoted to Hunan surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to Hunan surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 苗人籥留，命每年秋一赴苗疆撫慰邊人。

translations.literal: The Miao detained him and begged him to remain; he was ordered to visit the Miao frontier once each autumn to comfort the border people.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao begged him to stay; the court ordered him to visit the frontier once each autumn to comfort the border population.

sentences.zh: 鼐在苗疆，設木匭於門，訴者投牒其中，夜出閱之，黎明起視事，剖決立盡。

translations.literal: While Nai was in the Miao frontier, he set a wooden complaint box at his gate; litigants cast petitions into it; he went out at night to read them, rose at dawn to attend to business, and decided cases on the spot to completion.
translations.idiomatic: In the Miao country Nai placed a wooden complaint box at his gate. Petitioners dropped their papers inside; he read them at night, rose at dawn to hold court, and disposed of every case before the day was out.

sentences.zh: 兵民白事，直至榻前。

translations.literal: Soldiers and civilians reporting matters came straight to his couch.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers and civilians brought their business to his bedside.

sentences.zh: 及為按察使，一如同知時。

translations.literal: When he became surveillance commissioner, it was just as when he had been a subprefect.
translations.idiomatic: As surveillance commissioner he worked exactly as he had as subprefect.

sentences.zh: 下無壅情，事無不舉。

translations.literal: Below him no grievance was blocked; no affair went unhandled.
translations.idiomatic: No complaint was buried; no task left undone.

sentences.zh: 十五年，兼署布政使。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he concurrently served as acting provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he served concurrently as acting provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 十六年，卒於官，仁宗深悼惜，詔謂：「倚畀方隆，正欲簡任疆寄。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, he died in office; Emperor Renzong deeply mourned and lamented; the edict said: "Our reliance on him was just growing, and We were about to select him for a frontier post.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he died in office. Emperor Renzong mourned him deeply. The edict read: "Our reliance on him had only just deepened; We were on the point of entrusting him with a frontier command.

sentences.zh: 加恩贈巡撫銜，照贈官賜卹，賜祭一壇。

translations.literal: In grace let him be posthumously given the rank of provincial governor, with condolence according to the regulations for posthumous gifts, and one sacrificial altar bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Extend grace: posthumously grant him the rank of provincial governor, award the usual mourning gifts, and bestow one state sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 」苗疆建專祠，祀湖南名宦。

translations.literal: " A special shrine was built in the Miao frontier, enshrining him among Hunan's eminent officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao frontier raised a shrine to him, enrolling him among Hunan's eminent officials.

sentences.zh: 光緒中，追諡壯肅。

translations.literal: In the Guangxu reign, he was posthumously given the temple name Zhuangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Guangxu he received the posthumous name Zhuangsu ("Stalwart and Solemn").

sentences.zh: 初，鼐排眾議以事攻剿，為大吏所惎，將中以開邊釁罪。

translations.literal: Earlier, Nai had gone against majority opinion to pursue attack and suppression; he was envied by a grand official and was about to be charged centrally with the crime of provoking a border incident.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Nai had defied majority opinion to press the attack; a senior official bore him a grudge and nearly had him charged with provoking a border war.

sentences.zh: 監司阿意，旁掣其肘，鎮筸總兵富志那獨保全之。

translations.literal: Circuit intendants flattered their superiors' wishes and hampered him from the side; only Fu Zhina, commander-in-chief at Zhenqian, alone preserved him.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit officials curried favor and pulled at his sleeve; only Fu Zhina, the Zhenqian commander-in-chief, shielded him.

sentences.zh: 富志那從征金川，習知山碉設險之利，鼐實從受之，卒以成功。

translations.literal: Fu Zhina had campaigned in Jinchuan and was versed in the advantage of mountain blockhouses and strategic placement; Nai had in fact learned from him and in the end succeeded thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhina had fought in Jinchuan and knew the value of mountain blockhouses; Nai learned the method from him and succeeded by it.

sentences.zh: 鼐歿後，二妾寡居，饣於粥不給，其廉操尤著雲。

translations.literal: After Nai's death, his two concubines lived as widows without enough thin congee to eat; his integrity was especially renowned.
translations.idiomatic: After Nai died his two concubines lived as widows on thin gruel they could scarcely afford—proof of his integrity that men still speak of.

sentences.zh: 嚴如熤，字炳文，湖南溆浦人。

translations.literal: Yan Ruyi, courtesy name Bingwen, was a native of Xupu in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ruyi, style name Bingwen, was from Xupu in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 年十三，補諸生，舉優貢。

translations.literal: At age thirteen he qualified as a licentiate and was nominated as an outstanding tribute student.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he became a licentiate; later he was nominated as an outstanding tribute scholar.

sentences.zh: 研究輿圖、兵法、星卜之書，尤留心兵事。

translations.literal: He studied books on cartography, military science, and astrology and divination, paying special attention to military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He studied cartography, military science, and astrology, but kept his keenest eye on military affairs.

sentences.zh: 乾隆六十年，貴州苗亂，湖南巡撫姜晟闢佐幕，上平苗​​議十二事，言宜急复乾州，進永綏，與保靖、松桃、鎮筸聲勢可通。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year of Qianlong, when the Miao rebelled in Guizhou, Hunan provincial governor Jiang Sheng opened a staff post for him as aide; he submitted twelve proposals for pacifying the Miao, stating that Qianzhou should be recovered urgently, Yongshou advanced, and that with Baojing, Songtao, and Zhenqian the military dispositions could link up.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong year 60, when Guizhou's Miao rose in revolt, Hunan Governor Jiang Sheng took him onto his staff. Yan submitted twelve proposals for pacifying the Miao, urging the swift recovery of Qianzhou and an advance on Yongshou so that Baojing, Songtao, and Zhenqian could link their forces.

sentences.zh: 攻乾州道瀘溪，必先得大小章。

translations.literal: To attack Qianzhou by way of Luxi, one must first secure Daxiaozhang.
translations.idiomatic: The road to Qianzhou through Luxi required first winning over the Daxiaozhang.

sentences.zh: 大小章者，故土司遺民，名曰仡佬，驍健，與苗世仇。

translations.literal: Daxiaozhang were remnant people of the former native chieftaincies, called Gelao, fierce and strong, hereditary enemies of the Miao.
translations.idiomatic: The Daxiaozhang were descendants of former native chieftains, called Gelao—fierce fighters and hereditary enemies of the Miao.

sentences.zh: 如熤募能仡佬語者往，開示利害，挾其酋六人出，推誠與同臥起，乃送質，率其屬陽投乾州為內應，約一舉破賊，因黔師牽掣未果。

translations.literal: Ruyi recruited someone who could speak Gelao and sent him to explain advantage and harm; he brought out six of their chiefs, treated them with sincerity, sleeping and rising together, then sent hostages; he led their followers to feign surrender to Qianzhou as inside collaborators, planning to break the rebels in one stroke, but because Guizhou troops held them back it did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyi found a Gelao speaker and sent him to explain the stakes. He brought out six chiefs, shared their bed and board in token of trust, took hostages, and persuaded their people to feign submission to Qianzhou as inside allies—a plan to crush the rebels in one blow that Guizhou's armies held up and foiled.

sentences.zh: 次年，卒賴其眾，救兩鎮兵於河溪。

translations.literal: The next year, in the end relying on their forces, he rescued the troops of two garrisons at Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: The following year their warriors at last rescued two garrison forces at Hexi.

sentences.zh: 後復平隴，戰花園，皆為軍鋒。

translations.literal: Later, at the pacification of Long and the battle of Huayuan, they again served as the army's spearhead.
translations.idiomatic: They again led the van at the pacification of Long and the battle of Huayuan.

sentences.zh: 大小章於大府檄或不受，必得如熤手書始行雲。

translations.literal: Daxiaozhang might not accept a grand coordinator's dispatch, but would act only on receiving Ruyi's personal letter.
translations.idiomatic: The Daxiaozhang might ignore a grand coordinator's orders, but would move only on a personal letter from Ruyi.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶五年，舉孝廉方正。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiaqing, he was nominated as Filial and Incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing year 5 he was nominated as Filial and Incorrupt.

sentences.zh: 廷試平定川、楚、陝三省方略策，如熤對幾萬言，略謂：「軍興數載，師老財匱。

translations.literal: At the palace examination on strategy for pacifying Sichuan, Huguang, and Shaanxi, Ruyi answered in nearly ten thousand characters, stating in summary: "The war has lasted several years; the army is weary and the treasury exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: At the palace examination on strategy for pacifying Sichuan, Huguang, and Shaanxi, Ruyi wrote nearly ten thousand characters. In essence he argued: "The war has dragged on for years; the army is exhausted and the treasury empty.

sentences.zh: 以數万罷憊之眾，與猾賊追逐數千里長林深谷中。

translations.literal: With tens of thousands of worn-out troops, one chases cunning bandits for thousands of li through long forests and deep valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of spent soldiers are chasing cunning rebels through thousands of li of forest and ravine.

sentences.zh: 投誠之賊，無地安置，則已降复亂；

translations.literal: Bandits who have surrendered have no place to settle, and those who have already submitted rebel again;
translations.idiomatic: Surrendered rebels have nowhere to go, so men who have already submitted rise again;

sentences.zh: 流離之民，生活無資，則良亦從亂。

translations.literal: displaced civilians with no means of livelihood likewise join the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: and displaced civilians with no livelihood join them.

sentences.zh: 鄉勇戍卒，多遊手募充。

translations.literal: Local braves and garrison soldiers are mostly recruited idlers.
translations.idiomatic: Local militia and garrison troops are largely recruited from the idle and disorderly.

sentences.zh: 慮一旦兵撤餉停，則反思延亂。

translations.literal: Fearing that once troops are withdrawn and rations stop, they will in turn think of prolonging the chaos.
translations.idiomatic: Once the army withdraws and pay stops, they will have every reason to keep the turmoil alive.

sentences.zh: 如此，則亂何由弭？

translations.literal: In such circumstances, how can disorder be quelled?
translations.idiomatic: Under these conditions, how can rebellion ever end?

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為莫若仿古屯田之法。

translations.literal: This subject humbly considers that nothing is better than reviving the ancient garrison-farming method.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly believe the answer is to revive the ancient garrison-farming system.

sentences.zh: 三省自遭蹂躪，叛亡各產不下億萬畝，舉流民降賊之無歸、鄉勇戍卒之無業者，悉編入屯，團練捍衛，計可養勝兵數十萬。

translations.literal: The three provinces, since being ravaged, have had no less than hundreds of millions of mu from rebels and fugitives; enroll all displaced people and surrendered bandits without refuge, and local braves and garrison soldiers without occupation, entirely into garrisons, drill and defend them together, and it is estimated one could maintain several hundred thousand victorious troops.
translations.idiomatic: The three provinces, ravaged by war, hold hundreds of millions of mu abandoned by rebels and refugees. Enroll every homeless refugee, every surrendered bandit, every idle militiaman and discharged soldier into garrison colonies, drill them for defense, and you could maintain several hundred thousand effective troops.

sentences.zh: 餉省而兵增，化盜為民，計無逾此。

translations.literal: Rations saved while troops increase, turning bandits into civilians—no plan surpasses this.
translations.idiomatic: Payroll shrinks while strength grows; bandits become farmers. No policy surpasses it.

sentences.zh: 」仁宗親擢第一。

translations.literal: " Emperor Renzong personally ranked him first.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong ranked his paper first.

sentences.zh: 次日，召詣軍機處詢屯政，复條上十二事。

translations.literal: The next day he was summoned to the Grand Council to be questioned on garrison policy, and again submitted twelve items in detail.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was summoned to the Grand Council to discuss garrison policy and submitted twelve detailed proposals.

sentences.zh: 召見，以知縣發陝西。

translations.literal: On audience he was dispatched to Shaanxi as a county magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: After audience he was sent to Shaanxi as a county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 下其疏於三省大吏，令採行。

translations.literal: His memorial was sent down to the grand officials of the three provinces with orders to adopt it.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial went to the governors of all three provinces with orders to put it into practice.

sentences.zh: 六年，補洵陽，縣在萬山中，與湖北邊界相錯，兵賊往來如織。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed to Xunyang; the county lies among myriad mountains, its border interlocking with Hubei, with soldiers and bandits coming and going thick as weave.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he took Xunyang—a county lost in ten thousand hills, its border tangled with Hubei, soldiers and bandits crossing like shuttles on a loom.

sentences.zh: 時方厲行堅壁清野，如熤於築堡練團，措置尤力。

translations.literal: At the time the strict policy of fortified villages and cleared countryside was being enforced; Ruyi was especially forceful in building forts and drilling militia.
translations.idiomatic: The government was enforcing scorched-earth fortification; Ruyi threw himself especially hard into building forts and drilling militia.

sentences.zh: 賊至無可掠，去則抄其尾。

translations.literal: When bandits came there was nothing to plunder; when they left he struck their rear.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels arrived they found nothing to loot; when they withdrew he harried their rear.

sentences.zh: 又擇堅寨當衝者，儲糧供給官軍。

translations.literal: He also selected stout stockades blocking the main routes, storing grain to supply government troops.
translations.idiomatic: He stocked grain in strong stockades on the main routes to feed government troops.

sentences.zh: 徐天德、樊人傑敗於張家坪，因馬鞍寨阻其前，故不得竄。

translations.literal: Xu Tiande and Fan Renjie were defeated at Zhangjiaping; because Ma'an Stockade blocked their front, they could not break through.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Tiande and Fan Renjie were beaten at Zhangjiaping; Ma'an Stockade blocked their path and they could not escape.

sentences.zh: 楊遇春破張天倫，亦賴太平寨夾擊之力。

translations.literal: When Yang Yuchun defeated Zhang Tianlun, he likewise relied on the flanking power of Taiping Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yuchun's defeat of Zhang Tianlun likewise depended on a flanking strike from Taiping Stockade.

sentences.zh: 以功加知州銜，賜花翎。

translations.literal: For merit he was given the rank of subprefect and awarded the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he received the rank of subprefect and the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 八年，擊湖北逸匪於蜀河口，斬王祥，擒方孝德，晉秩同知直隸州。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he attacked Hubei fugitive bandits at Shuhekou, beheaded Wang Xiang, captured Fang Xiaode, and was promoted in rank to subprefect of Zhili Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 he attacked Hubei fugitive bandits at Shuhekou, beheaded Wang Xiang, captured Fang Xiaode, and was promoted to subprefect of Zhili Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 新設定遠廳，即以如熤補授。

translations.literal: The newly established Dingyuan Department was thereupon filled by appointing Ruyi.
translations.idiomatic: When Dingyuan Department was newly created, Ruyi was appointed to fill the post.

sentences.zh: 九年，建新城，复於西南百餘裡黎壩、漁渡壩築二石城為犄角。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he built a new city, and also at Liba and Yuduba over a hundred li to the southwest erected two stone cities as horn pincers.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9 he built a new city and, a hundred li southwest at Liba and Yuduba, two stone forts as pincers.

sentences.zh: 治團如洵陽，賊至輒殲，先後擒陳心元、馮世週。

translations.literal: He organized militia as at Xunyang; when bandits came they were always destroyed; he successively captured Chen Xinyuan and Feng Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He organized militia as at Xunyang; rebels who came were destroyed; he captured Chen Xinyuan and Feng Shizhou.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，大吏議留任，辭不可，服闋，十三年，補潼關廳。

translations.literal: When his mother died he was in mourning; grand officials discussed retaining him in office, but he declined and could not be persuaded; when mourning ended, in the thirteenth year he was appointed to Tongguan Department.
translations.idiomatic: On his mother's death superiors urged him to stay in office; he refused. After mourning, in year 13 he took Tongguan Department.

sentences.zh: 尋擢漢中知府。

translations.literal: Soon after he was promoted to prefect of Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was promoted to prefect of Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 兵燹後，民困兵驕，散勇逸匪，心猶未革。

translations.literal: After the fires of war, the people were destitute and the soldiers arrogant; discharged braves and fugitive bandits had not yet reformed their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: After the war the people were ruined, the troops insolent, and discharged braves and roaming bandits had not yet changed their ways.

sentences.zh: 如熤聯營伍，立保甲，治堡寨，問民疾苦。

translations.literal: Ruyi linked camp units, established baojia household registers, repaired stockades, and inquired into the people's hardships.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyi reorganized the camps, set up baojia registers, repaired stockades, and went among the people to hear their grievances.

sentences.zh: 興勸農事，行區田法，教紡織，使務本計。

translations.literal: He promoted agriculture, implemented the field-allotment method, taught spinning and weaving, and made people attend to fundamental livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted farming, introduced field-allotment farming, taught spinning and weaving, and turned people back to honest livelihood.

sentences.zh: 修復褒城山河堰及城固五門、楊填二堰，各灌田數万畝，他小堰百餘，皆履勘濬治，水利普興。

translations.literal: He restored the Shanhe Weir at Baocheng and the Wumen and Yangtian weirs at Chenggu, each irrigating tens of thousands of mu; over a hundred smaller weirs besides—all were surveyed on foot, dredged, and repaired, and waterworks flourished everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: He restored Baocheng's Shanhe Weir and Chenggu's Wumen and Yangtian weirs, each watering tens of thousands of mu, and personally surveyed and dredged more than a hundred smaller weirs until irrigation flourished throughout the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 复漢中書院，親臨講授。

translations.literal: He restored the Hanzhong Academy and personally came to lecture.
translations.idiomatic: He revived the Hanzhong Academy and taught there in person.

sentences.zh: 於華州渭南開諭悍回，縛獻亡命數十人；

translations.literal: At Weinan in Huazhou he openly instructed the fierce Hui, bound and presented several tens of fugitives;
translations.idiomatic: At Weinan in Huazhou he persuaded the unruly Hui factions and delivered several dozen fugitives bound;

sentences.zh: 於寧羌解散湖北流民；

translations.literal: At Ningqiang he dispersed the Hubei drift population;
translations.idiomatic: at Ningqiang he sent home displaced people from Hubei;

sentences.zh: 於城固擒教首陳恆義：皆治渠魁，寬脅從。
