translations.literal: At Chenggu he captured the sect leader Chen Hengyi: in every case he punished the ringleaders and was lenient to those coerced to follow.
translations.idiomatic: at Chenggu he seized the sect leader Chen Hengyi—in each case punishing the chiefs while sparing those who had been compelled to follow.

sentences.zh: 令行禁止，人心帖服，南山遂大定。

translations.literal: Orders ran and prohibitions were enforced; hearts submitted; the Southern Mountains were thereby greatly pacified.
translations.idiomatic: His orders were obeyed and his prohibitions heeded; the people submitted, and the Southern Mountains were finally at peace.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，擢陝安道。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang, he was promoted to Shaan-An Circuit Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In 1821 he was promoted to intendant of the Shaan-An circuit.

sentences.zh: 會廷議川、楚、陝邊防建設事宜，下三省察勘，以如熤任其事，週曆相度，析官移治，增營改汛，建城口、白河、磚坪、太平、佛坪五廳，移駐文武。

translations.literal: When the court deliberated on Sichuan-Huguang-Shaanxi border defense construction, it ordered the three provinces to survey; Ruyi was put in charge, toured and measured throughout, divided offices and moved administrations, increased garrisons and changed posts, established the five departments of Chengkou, Baihe, Zhuanping, Taiping, and Foping, and moved civil and military officials to garrison them.
translations.idiomatic: When the court took up border defenses along the Sichuan-Huguang-Shaanxi frontier, it commissioned surveys in all three provinces and put Ruyi in charge. He traveled the region end to end, reorganized county seats, reinforced garrison posts, created five new subprefectures at Chengkou, Baihe, Zhuanping, Taiping, and Foping, and redeployed civil and military officials to staff them.

sentences.zh: 奏上，報可。

translations.literal: He memorialized upward; approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial was submitted and approved.

sentences.zh: 如熤嘗言：「山內州縣距省遠，多推諉牽掣。

translations.literal: Ruyi once said: "The counties within the mountains are far from the provincial capitals and often pass blame and pull in opposite directions.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyi once argued: "Mountain counties lie far from provincial capitals, and officials endlessly shift blame and thwart one another.

sentences.zh: 宜仿古梁州自為一道及明鄖陽巡撫之制，專設大員鎮撫，割三省州縣以附益之，庶勢專權一，可百世無患。

translations.literal: It would be fitting to follow the ancient model of Liangzhou as its own circuit and the Ming system of the Xunyang grand coordinator, establishing a dedicated senior official to pacify and control, carving out counties of the three provinces to augment it, so that authority would be unified in one hand and no trouble for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: We should revive the ancient Liang circuit and the Ming office of Xunyang grand coordinator—a senior official devoted solely to the region, with counties carved from all three provinces placed under him—so power would be concentrated and the trouble ended for generations.

sentences.zh: 」以更張重大，未竟其議。

translations.literal: " Because the restructuring was weighty, his proposal was never carried through.
translations.idiomatic: " The scale of reform was deemed too great, and his plan never went forward.

sentences.zh: 三年，宣宗以如熤在陝年久，熟於南山情形，任事以來，地方安靖，特詔嘉獎，加按察使銜，以示旌異。

translations.literal: In the third year the Xuanzong Emperor, because Ruyi had been long in Shaanxi and was thoroughly familiar with Southern Mountain conditions, and since taking office the region had been tranquil, issued a special edict of praise and added the rank of surveillance commissioner as a mark of distinction.
translations.idiomatic: In 1823 the Daoguang Emperor noted that Ruyi had served many years in Shaanxi, knew the Southern Mountains intimately, and had kept the region quiet throughout his tenure. He issued a special commendation and granted him the nominal rank of surveillance commissioner as exceptional recognition.

sentences.zh: 巡撫盧坤尤重之，採其議增廳治於盩厔、洋縣界，增營汛於商州及略陽；

translations.literal: Governor Lu Kun especially valued him, adopted his proposal to add a department seat on the boundary of Zhouzhi and Yang County, and increased garrison posts at Shangzhou and Lueyang;
translations.idiomatic: Governor Lu Kun prized him highly, followed his advice to establish a new subprefecture on the Zhouzhi–Yangxian border, and reinforced garrisons at Shangzhou and Lueyang;

sentences.zh: 檄勘全秦水利，於灃、涇、滻、渭諸川，鄭白、龍首諸渠，規畫俱備。

translations.literal: He dispatched orders to survey all Shaanxi waterworks; on the Fen, Jing, Chan, and Wei rivers and the Zheng-Bai and Longshou canals, plans were all complete.
translations.idiomatic: he ordered a province-wide survey of irrigation, and drew up comprehensive plans for the Fen, Jing, Chan, and Wei rivers and the Zheng-Bai and Longshou canals.

sentences.zh: 社倉、義學，亦以次推行。

translations.literal: Community granaries and charity schools were also rolled out in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Community granaries and charity schools were introduced in turn.

sentences.zh: 五年，擢貴州按察使，未到官。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was promoted to Guizhou surveillance commissioner but did not reach his post.
translations.idiomatic: In 1825 he was promoted to surveillance commissioner of Guizhou but never took up the appointment.

sentences.zh: 六年，入覲，仍調陝西，抵任數日而卒，贈布政使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he went to audience, was still transferred to Shaanxi, reached his post for several days and died, and was posthumously enfeoffed as provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: In 1826 he was called to court, reassigned to Shaanxi, took office, and died within days; he was posthumously granted the rank of provincial treasurer.

sentences.zh: 陝民請比硃邑桐鄉故事，留葬南山，勿得，乃請祀名宦。

translations.literal: Shaanxi people requested following the precedent of Zhu Yi of Tongxiang to keep his burial in the Southern Mountains; this was not granted, and they then requested enshrinement in the shrine of eminent officials.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shaanxi asked, by the example of Zhu Yi of Tongxiang, to bury him in the Southern Mountains; when refused, they petitioned for his place in the shrine of distinguished officials.

sentences.zh: 湖南亦祀鄉賢。

translations.literal: Hunan also enshrined him among local worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan enshrined him among its local worthies as well.

sentences.zh: 如熤自為縣令至臬司，皆出特擢。

translations.literal: From magistrate to provincial judge, Ruyi's every promotion came by special selection.
translations.idiomatic: Every step from county magistrate to provincial judge, Ruyi rose by special appointment.

sentences.zh: 在漢中十餘年不調，得成其鎮撫南山之功。

translations.literal: More than ten years in Hanzhong without transfer allowed him to complete his work of pacifying the Southern Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten years in Hanzhong without reassignment let him finish pacifying the Southern Mountains.

sentences.zh: 宣宗每論疆吏才，必首及之。

translations.literal: Whenever the Xuanzong Emperor discussed frontier officials' talent, he always mentioned Ruyi first.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Daoguang Emperor spoke of frontier talent, Ruyi's name came first.

sentences.zh: 將大用，已不及待。

translations.literal: He was about to be greatly employed, but death could not wait.
translations.idiomatic: The throne meant to promote him further, but death came too soon.

sentences.zh: 為人性豪邁，去邊幅，泊榮利，視之如田夫野老。

translations.literal: By nature he was bold and expansive, shed formal trappings, was indifferent to glory and profit, and comported himself like a farmer or rustic elder.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was bold and unceremonious, indifferent to rank and gain, and comported himself like an ordinary peasant.

sentences.zh: 於輿地險要，如聚米畫沙。

translations.literal: On dangerous terrain in geography, it was like piling millet or drawing on sand.
translations.idiomatic: On strategic terrain he could lay out the lie of the land as easily as piling grain or tracing lines in sand.

sentences.zh: 所規畫常在數十年外，措施略見所著書。

translations.literal: What he planned often lay decades ahead; measures are briefly visible in his written works.
translations.idiomatic: His designs looked decades ahead; his practical measures are outlined in his books.

sentences.zh: 嘗佐那彥成籌海寇，有洋防備覽；

translations.literal: He once assisted Na Yancheng in planning against sea bandits and wrote the Maritime Defense Survey;
translations.idiomatic: He assisted Na Yancheng against coastal pirates and wrote the Maritime Defense Survey;

sentences.zh: 佐姜晟籌苗疆，有苗防備覽；

translations.literal: He assisted Jiang Sheng in planning the Miao frontier and wrote the Miao Frontier Defense Survey;
translations.idiomatic: he helped Jiang Sheng on the Miao frontier and wrote the Miao Frontier Defense Survey;

sentences.zh: 佐傅鼐籌屯田，有屯防書。

translations.literal: He assisted Fu Nai in planning military colonies and wrote the Colony Defense Treatise.
translations.idiomatic: he assisted Fu Nai on military colonies and wrote the Colony Defense Treatise.

sentences.zh: 又有三省邊防備覽，漢江南北、三省山內各圖，漢中府誌及樂園詩文集。

translations.literal: He also had the Three-Provinces Border Defense Survey, maps of north and south of the Han River and within the mountains of the three provinces, the Hanzhong Prefecture Gazetteer, and the Leyuan poetry and prose collection.
translations.idiomatic: He also produced the Three-Provinces Border Defense Survey, maps of the Han valley and the interior mountains, the Hanzhong Gazetteer, and the Leyuan collected writings.

sentences.zh: 子正基，原名芝，字山舫。

translations.literal: His son Zheng Ji, original name Zhi, courtesy name Shanfang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zheng Ji, born Zhi, style name Shanfang.

sentences.zh: 副貢生。

translations.literal: A second-class tribute student.
translations.idiomatic: He held the rank of deputy tribute student.

sentences.zh: 少隨父練習吏事。

translations.literal: In youth he followed his father in practicing official affairs.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he trained in administration at his father's side.

sentences.zh: 道光中，官河南知縣，有聲。

translations.literal: In the Daoguang era he served as Henan county magistrate with reputation.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daoguang reign he served as magistrate in Henan and won a strong reputation.

sentences.zh: 擢鄭州知州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to magistrate of Zhengzhou Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to prefect of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 治賈魯河，息水患。

translations.literal: He managed the Jia and Lu Rivers and quelled flood calamity.
translations.idiomatic: He improved the Jia-Lu River works and ended the flooding.

sentences.zh: 河決開封，正基佐守護。

translations.literal: When the Yellow River burst its banks at Kaifeng, Zheng Ji assisted in defense.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River broke at Kaifeng, Zheng Ji aided the emergency defense.

sentences.zh: 治河兵獄，雪其冤，得河兵死力，城賴以完。

translations.literal: He handled a criminal case among river troops, cleared their injustice, won the river soldiers' utmost loyalty, and the city was thereby preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: He investigated a scandal among the river-defense troops, cleared the men's names, and won such loyalty that the city held.

sentences.zh: 母憂歸，服闋，補奉天復州。

translations.literal: On his mother's mourning he returned home; when mourning ended he was appointed to Fuzhou in Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death he retired for mourning, then was appointed to Fuzhou in Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 興屯練，捕盜有法，民殺盜者勿論。

translations.literal: He promoted colony militia training; catching bandits had method; if common people killed bandits they were not prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: He raised militia on the colonies, policed bandits systematically, and exempted civilians who killed robbers from prosecution.

sentences.zh: 奉天治吏素弛，府尹下所屬，以正基為法，盜風為戢。

translations.literal: Fengtian governance of officials had long been lax; the prefect sent his subordinates to take Zheng Ji as model, and banditry was curbed.
translations.idiomatic: Fengtian had long been slack in controlling officials; the prefect held Zheng Ji up as the standard for his subordinates, and banditry subsided.

sentences.zh: 引疾去。

translations.literal: He cited illness and left office.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 江南大吏疏調，擢授常州知府。

translations.literal: A senior Jiangnan official memorialized to transfer him; he was promoted and appointed Changzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: A senior Jiangnan official requested him by memorial, and he was appointed prefect of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，大水，勘災勤至，郡人感之，輸錢二十餘萬助賑，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year great flood came; his disaster survey was diligent and thorough; the prefecture people were moved, contributed more than two hundred thousand in cash to aid relief, and very many were wholly saved alive.
translations.idiomatic: In 1849 a great flood struck; his relief surveys were tireless, and moved by his effort the prefecture donated more than two hundred thousand strings of cash for famine relief, saving countless lives.

sentences.zh: 累署淮揚道、按察使。

translations.literal: He repeatedly acted as Huai-Yang Circuit intendant and surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as acting intendant of the Huai-Yang circuit and surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，侍郎曾國籓、呂賢基交章薦之，命赴廣西治軍需，授右江道。

translations.literal: Early in Xianfeng, Vice Ministers Zeng Guofan and Lü Xianji jointly memorialized to recommend him; he was ordered to Guangxi to manage military supplies and appointed Right River Circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianfeng reign Vice Ministers Zeng Guofan and Lü Xianji recommended him in joint memorials; he was sent to Guangxi to manage army supplies and made intendant of the Right River circuit.

sentences.zh: 擢河南布政使，留廣西。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Henan provincial treasurer but retained in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to treasurer of Henan but kept on in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 時粵匪披猖，將帥齟《齒吾》，師久無功。

translations.literal: At the time Guangdong bandits ran rampant; commanders were at odds; the army was long without success.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi rebels were rampant, commanders feuded, and the campaign dragged on without victory.

sentences.zh: 正基曲為調和，疏論其事，謂：「師克在和，事期共濟。

translations.literal: Zheng Ji tactfully mediated and in a memorial discussed the matter, saying: "An army conquers through harmony; affairs look to mutual support.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Ji worked to mediate and memorialized on the crisis: "Victory depends on unity, and the campaign requires shared effort.

sentences.zh: 統兵大帥與地方大吏，宜定紛更不齊之勢，聯疏闊難合之情。

translations.literal: The supreme field commanders and local grand officials should settle the disorder of uneven policies and join estranged sentiments hard to reconcile.
translations.idiomatic: Field commanders and provincial governors must settle their clashing policies and bridge the distance between them.

sentences.zh: 布德信以服人心，明功罪以揚士氣。

translations.literal: Spread virtue and trust to win people's hearts; clarify merit and guilt to raise soldiers' spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Win hearts through integrity and trust; make merit and blame clear to lift morale.

sentences.zh: 勿因賊盛而生推諉，勿因兵單而務自救，勿以小忿而不為應援，勿以偶挫而坐觀成敗。

translations.literal: Do not because the rebels are strong produce mutual buck-passing; do not because troops are few devote yourself only to self-preservation; do not for a small grievance refuse mutual reinforcement; do not for an occasional setback sit watching success or failure.
translations.idiomatic: Do not use the enemy's strength as an excuse to shift blame; do not hoard your few troops for self-preservation alone; do not withhold aid over petty quarrels; do not watch from the sidelines after a single setback.

sentences.zh: 庶逆氛可殄，大功可成。

translations.literal: Then perhaps the rebellious aura can be extinguished and the great task accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Only then can the rebellion be crushed and final victory won.

sentences.zh: 」時以為讜言。

translations.literal: " At the time this was regarded as forthright counsel.
translations.idiomatic: " His contemporaries hailed it as forthright counsel.

sentences.zh: 二年，桂林圍解，賜花翎。

translations.literal: In the second year the siege of Guilin was lifted; he was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In 1852, when the siege of Guilin was lifted, he was awarded the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 尋隨大軍赴湖北，時武昌初复，命馳往撫卹難民，署湖北布政使。

translations.literal: Soon he followed the main army to Hubei; at the time Wuchang had just been retaken; he was ordered to hurry there to comfort refugees and acted as Hubei provincial treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: He soon followed the main force to Hubei; Wuchang had just been recovered, and he was dispatched to care for refugees as acting treasurer of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 調廣東，复赴廣西清覈軍需。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Guangdong, then again went to Guangxi to audit military supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Guangdong, he returned again to Guangxi to audit army supplies.

sentences.zh: 內召授通政副使，遷通政使。

translations.literal: Summoned within to be appointed vice commissioner of the Transmission Office, then transferred to transmission commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to the capital, he was made vice commissioner of the Transmission Office and then commissioner.

sentences.zh: 七年，引疾歸，卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he cited illness and returned home, then died.
translations.idiomatic: In 1857 he retired for illness, returned home, and died.

sentences.zh: 論曰：亂之所由起與亂之所由平，亦在民之能治否耳。

translations.literal: The commentator says: The arising of disorder and the pacifying of disorder likewise depend on whether the people can be governed or not.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Whether turmoil breaks out and whether it ends both turn on whether the people can be well governed.

sentences.zh: 教匪起於官逼民叛，其間獨一得民心之劉清，卒賴以招撫，助誅剿之成功。

translations.literal: The sect rebels arose from officials pressing the people until they rebelled; among them only Liu Qing, who won popular hearts, in the end was relied upon for pacification through inducement, aiding the success of suppression and destruction.
translations.idiomatic: The sect rebels rose because officials drove the people to revolt; only Liu Qing, who won the people's trust, could in the end pacify them by persuasion and help complete their destruction.

sentences.zh: 徵苗頻煩大兵，而未杜亂源，傅鼐乃以一廳一道之力，剿撫兼施，岩疆綏定。

translations.literal: Miao campaigns frequently taxed great armies yet did not cut off the source of disorder; Fu Nai then with the strength of one department and one circuit combined suppression and pacification, and the stony frontier was soothed and settled.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigns against the Miao repeatedly mobilized large armies without stopping the trouble at its source; Fu Nai, with only one subprefecture and one circuit to work with, combined force and conciliation until the rugged frontier was secure.

sentences.zh: 南山善後，嚴如熤始終其事，化榛莽為桑麻。

translations.literal: Southern Mountain aftermath—Yan Ruyi saw it through from start to finish, transforming brambled wilderness into mulberry and hemp.
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Mountains' recovery was Yan Ruyi's work from beginning to end—turning wilderness into farmland.

sentences.zh: 此其功皆在一時節鉞之上，光於史策矣。

translations.literal: These achievements all stood above the military authority of their day and shine upon the historical record.
translations.idiomatic: Their achievements exceeded those of the generals of their day and deserve to blaze from the historical record.
